html:
Bangui, the capital of the Central African Republic, was founded in 1889 as a French post on the Ubangi river, below rapids that block boats from going further upstream.

The river was the colony's only good route out, by boat to Brazzaville and then by rail to the sea, so the post grew into the capital of Ubangi-Shari. Across the river lies the Congo.

It was the stage for Bokassa's court and his coronation, and in the civil war for the Séléka capture of 2013 and the killings that followed. Today it is home to most of the country's government, business and schools.
sum: Bangui, the capital of the Central African Republic, was founded in 1889 as a French post on the Ubangi river, below rapids that block boats from going further upstream.
